prompts.pressed-in-paper:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic, production-quality desktop website UI design for Luis Augusto's interactive digital business card. One independent concept, one focused primary screen, not a collage or multi-option presentation. Target dimensions: 1440 x 1024. No browser or device chrome. Beautiful crafted web art direction with clear hierarchy, strong typography, generous spacing, readable text, no clipped content. The user explicitly wants a physically recognizable business card as the central interactive object, with delight and wow factor.
Reference image 1 is the current live site; use it for identity and essential content, but radically explore a new design direction. Current source uses Public Sans and IBM Plex Mono, warm off-white or charcoal and amber; varying these is explicitly wanted. Reference image 2 is the user's portrait; when a portrait appears faithfully preserve his face, hair and appearance. Do not invent a new person.
Required exact public content: "Luis Augusto", "Product & Growth Engineering", "Sacramento, CA", "hello@luis.app". Main action "Save my contact" must be visible and clear. Supporting contact links can be a compact text row: "GitHub", "LinkedIn", "Email". A small "Writing" link is allowed. No invented clients, metrics, credentials, article titles, statuses, marketing claims, or lorem ipsum. No dates. Focus on meeting Luis and saving his contact, not a dashboard. Contact links and save button should not depend on discovering a hidden gesture. At most two fonts. Avoid nested panel UI, extraneous navigation, or huge marketing headline separate from the name on the card. Every direction should feel like a complete, intentional website. Put a small interaction hint under the card, not presentation annotations.
Concept name: Pressed in Paper. Design the page like a premium stationery studio photographed on a warm ivory desk, minimal but deeply tactile. A large landscape business card, roughly 760 x 430, is positioned centrally with a gentle 5-degree rotation and credible paper thickness, uncoated cotton fibers, softly debossed dark-olive ink and a thin ochre dyed edge. Beautiful natural raking sunlight from upper left and a believable soft paper shadow; do not overdo photoreal desk props. This is an interactive website, not a print mockup advertisement. Put a tiny LA wordmark at top left of the web page and Sacramento, CA at top right. On the business card: oversized refined dark espresso serif "Luis Augusto" split into two handsome lines, Product & Growth Engineering in small spaced sans, a tiny tasteful portrait at upper right using the supplied photo, contact email at lower left and a subtle flip arrow at lower right. Use warm russet or mustard for just one detail. The card is the hero and the typography is stunning. Below the object place an accessible dark olive "Save my contact" button and compact GitHub / LinkedIn / Email links. Subtle under-card hint exactly "Pick it up. Turn it over." At bottom right a tiny Writing link. Maintain lots of breathing room. All text rendered crisply and correct. No glowing effects, no glass, no neon, no rounded nested UI cards. The wow comes from hyper-tactile material, shadow, elegant typography, and the suggestion of picking up and flipping a real business card. Do not place the concept title in the design.

Concept name: Prismatic. A radically futuristic, art-directed luxury digital business card website on a nearly black charcoal background, free of desktop props. Hero is a single giant landscape thin smoked titanium card floating at a subtle 3D angle in the center, ratio about 1.65:1, with subtly rounded corners and one beautifully iridescent foil ribbon bending diagonally across its right half. Spectral colors lime, icy cyan, soft peach and hot violet are confined to the foil texture and hairline edge; the page itself is restrained charcoal. Micro-etched fine concentric guilloche lines across the metal surface, physically plausible oil-slick shimmer, a precisely rendered edge highlight. Left-aligned huge clean grotesk white "Luis Augusto" across two lines occupies the left half of the card, with "Product & Growth Engineering" beneath. Tiny "Sacramento, CA" at the top edge and "hello@luis.app" at bottom left. Small tasteful inset round supplied portrait near top right, with a thin silver border. No payment chip, no credit card numbers, no fabricated status or membership credentials. Top left of page a tiny white "LA" typographic mark. Card sits above a soft pool of charcoal light, no bright background gradients or random sci-fi environment. Below card, precise instruction "Move to catch the light. Drag to rotate." Below that, an elegant off-white "Save my contact" button; GitHub, LinkedIn, Email in quiet gray compact row and small Writing at bottom right. This should feel like interacting with a prized holographic object, not a generic SaaS page. Strong visual contrast, high readability, enormous negative space, sharp material realism. Use Public Sans with IBM Plex Mono for metadata. No concept title visible, no explanatory presentation labels.

Concept name: The Sleeve. Design a distinctly playful editorial website with a saturated tomato red full-bleed canvas (#e3402e), warm cream and ink navy typography, completely different from a centered floating metallic card. One large composition in the middle: a vermilion red paper sleeve with a half-moon thumb notch at its right edge, and a warm pale-yellow landscape business card sliding horizontally out toward the right. Show the pulled-out position so the entire user's name and portrait are fully readable on the exposed card area. Overall composition spans roughly 1050 px horizontally but has ample page margins. The sleeve is left-center, darker red than background, realistic folded seams and very subtle soft shadows. Sleeve front displays a wonderfully large cream lowercase "hello." and tiny cream "A card from Luis". The cream business card extends to the right and is slightly lifted at its right corner. Its compact three-column composition: supplied portrait as a vertical postage-stamp-like rectangle at top right, bold dark-navy sans-serif "Luis Augusto" at top left with a friendly chunky typeface, "Product & Growth Engineering" below, "Sacramento, CA" in small sans above name, "hello@luis.app" along bottom. The card has an obvious small exposed grip tab labelled "PULL" on the right end, no unrelated stickers. Main web page top left very small cream "LUIS AUGUSTO" and top right "SACRAMENTO, CA". Beneath the central object place the hint "Pull to say hello." A cream pill "Save my contact" is always visible below, and a restrained cream GitHub / LinkedIn / Email text row. Writing small at bottom right. Elegant editorial use of scale, clever physical interaction, tactile paper craft, crisp typography and strong personality. No giant repeated marketing headline, no multiple cards, no glass, no gradients, no foil, no desk props. No concept title visible.

Concept name: Swiss Fold. Create a striking experimental Swiss graphic design website, very modern, typographic and highly intentional. Palette: electric ultramarine blue (#203de2), sharp acid yellow (#edfa58), pale cool gray. Full page background pale cool gray, small black "LA / CONTACT" top left, "Sacramento, CA" top right. Main object is an extraordinary partially unfolded accordion business card made of THREE PHYSICALLY CONNECTED panels; this is ONE folded card, not three floating UI cards. Full width about 1000px, with left panel blue, middle acid yellow, right blue, panels shown in a shallow zigzag perspective with precise hinge creases and real fine paper edges. Left panel has massive condensed sans typography "Luis" in yellow and "Augusto" beneath, carefully fit; this makes the name the dominant graphic element. Middle yellow panel has "Product & Growth Engineering" in bold blue, "Sacramento, CA" in small blue, a small square supplied portrait anchored at the bottom, no fake icon illustration. Right blue panel has beautiful well-spaced yellow contact rows "hello@luis.app", "GitHub", "LinkedIn", "Writing", each with a small arrow; these are typography directly on the panel, no nested buttons. In the background only a faint simple baseline grid at page bottom, lots of calm whitespace. Under folded object: compact black text "A little more on the inside." and a small visible "Unfold" control with directional arrow. Persistent lower left ultramarine "Save my contact" rectangular button aligned to the object left edge, supporting Email link. The page feels like an interactive piece of contemporary graphic design and folds flat into a pocket-size card on click, with real 3D hinges. Scale must fit cleanly, excellent readability, no clipped letters. No holographic colors, no shadows other than precise fold shadows, no desk props, no round pill UI. Two fonts max, bold condensed grotesk and clean utility sans. No concept name or presentation headings.

Concept name: Pocket Deck. Design a delightfully playful, sophisticated interactive contact-card website with a pale pistachio-green full-page background, a dark forest-green ink color, dusty pink, butter yellow, and cream card stocks. This is a distinctly different composition: a compact fan of THREE SEPARATE VERTICAL tactile cards centered slightly right on the page, like a small deck of beautifully printed personal cards casually spread by hand. Main foremost portrait card about 350px wide by 480px tall, cream with dark forest-green text, slightly rotated clockwise, with the supplied person's real portrait in a large softly rounded rectangular photo occupying its upper half. Below the photo, handsome large friendly serif "Luis Augusto", "Product & Growth Engineering" in compact sans and "Sacramento, CA" in tiny sans. Rounded physical card corners and printed thick colored edges. Behind it, a dusty pink card fanned out to the left and rotated anticlockwise has the exposed heading "Writing" and very subtle printed horizontal ruled lines; a pale butter-yellow card fanned to the right has the exposed heading "Elsewhere" and small GitHub and LinkedIn text visible toward its outer edge. Do not fabricate article titles or additional biography. These are the ONLY cards. The deck looks physically draggable and springy, with small realistic layered shadows.
To the left of the deck on the same page, put a beautifully spaced modest editorial text group: small uppercase "NICE TO MEET YOU", a large lowercase "Take a card." in elegant dark-green serif, and a small email "hello@luis.app". Beneath that, a dark-green rectangular button with rounded corners saying "Save my contact" and a compact GitHub / LinkedIn / Email row. Keep this text block substantially smaller than the deck hero. Top left small LA typographic monogram, top right Sacramento, CA. Below the deck a clearly readable hint "Swipe through. Find your next connection." and a compact accessible "Previous" and "Next" pair, without circular pagination dots. Design should communicate fan-out on hover, swipe to bring one card forward, satisfying magnetic snap back; all without motion lines or illustrated hands. It is a polished website screenshot, not a diagram. Calm botanical palette, friendship and curiosity, bold enough to be memorable, impeccable type scale and generous whitespace. Avoid desk props, foil, neon, card sleeves, accordion folds, dashboard panels, excessive ornamental stickers. No presentation annotations or concept title.
